speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with a recent history of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better assess your condition, have you noticed any specific changes in your skin, such as blisters, peeling, or a "slapped cheek" appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The combination of a one-week prodrome of flu-like symptoms followed by a pruritic rash that appeared on the face (sparing the perioral area) and then spread to the trunk and extremities is classic for this condition. No further testing or images are required for this clinical presentation.
